conventions.convention: For U = Rⁿ ∖ {0}, n ≥ 1, dilation means tρ(φ) = ρ⁻ⁿt(φ(·/ρ)), with ρ > 0. For a regular distribution this corresponds to g(x) becoming g(ρx). The same convention applies on all of Rⁿ.

Scaling degree is the infimum of real ω for which ρ^ωtρ tends to zero on every fixed test as ρ decreases to zero. The empty admissible set has infimum +∞; an admissible set containing every real exponent has infimum −∞. Finite scaling degree means a real value.

The uniform scaling estimate assumes AC. The proof obtains DC and Countable Choice from AC and applies the published Baire theorem to the complete fixed-support test space. Downstream extension and classification results retain AC explicitly.

The extension family contains extensions of exactly the punctured distribution's scaling degree δ. For δ ≥ n the allowed delta-derivative orders are |α| ≤ floor(δ − n); for δ < n the family is a singleton. At δ = n only a multiple of δ₀ is allowed.

The anomaly uses the Euclidean kernel u(x) = 1/(16π⁴|x|⁴), one fixed compact smooth cutoff χ equal to one near zero, and subtraction χ(μx)φ(0). Its scale difference has positive coefficient: Tμ − Tν = (8π²)⁻¹ log(μ/ν)δ₀. Exact homogeneity means ρ⁴Tρ = T.
The power-kernel example permits every real δ ≤ n, assigns gδ(0) = 0 without affecting integrals, and distinguishes the locally integrable case δ < n from logarithmic divergence at δ = n.

load_bearing.statement: For t ∈ D′(Rⁿ ∖ {0}), define tρ(φ) = ρ⁻ⁿt(φ(·/ρ)) and sd₀(t) = inf{ω ∈ R : ρ^ωtρ → 0 on every fixed test as ρ ↓ 0}. An extension is a distribution on Rⁿ restricting to t on the punctured domain.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let n ≥ 1, U = Rⁿ ∖ {0}, and let t ∈ D′(U) have finite real scaling degree δ = sd₀(t). Then there exists T ∈ D′(Rⁿ) such that T|U = t and sd₀(T) = δ. The result applies to arbitrary distributions with finite real scaling degree; it assumes no smooth kernel or pointwise product representation.

Assume AC. For a punctured distribution t of finite real scaling degree δ, its exact-degree extension family Eδ(t) is nonempty. It is a singleton if δ < n. If δ ≥ n and k = floor(δ − n), then for every T₀ ∈ Eδ(t), Eδ(t) = T₀ + span_C{∂^αδ₀ : |α| ≤ k}.

Assume AC. If t ∈ D′(Rⁿ ∖ {0}) has finite real scaling degree δ, then for every compact K in the punctured domain and every real ω > δ there are m ≥ 0 and C < ∞ such that |tρ(ψ)| ≤ Cρ⁻ωp_m(ψ) for all 0 < ρ ≤ 1 and ψ ∈ D_K.

Assume AC. For u(x) = 1/(16π⁴|x|⁴) on punctured R⁴ and a compact smooth χ equal to one near zero, Tμ(φ) = ∫[φ(x) − χ(μx)φ(0)]/(16π⁴|x|⁴) d⁴x is an extension of scaling degree 4 for every μ > 0. For μ, ν > 0, Tμ − Tν = (8π²)⁻¹log(μ/ν)δ₀. No scaling-degree-4 extension of u is exactly homogeneous.
